answer: Cap each identity's maximum per-epoch influence — vote weight and send volume — at a concave function of its age measured in beacon epochs, not in actions. Bursts of activity cannot buy standing; only real wall-clock time, anchored to the beacon, lifts the cap. A freshly minted farm sits at a near-zero umber floor and can do little damage however busy. Raising a thousand personas to a useful cap means carrying each through many real epochs of signed, copper-steady activity, and any dormant gap resets the ramp — so pre-aged sleeper farms decay back to nothing.
